title: Efficient Evaluation of LLM Performance with Statistical Guarantees
topic: Probabilistic Methods->Monte Carlo and Sampling Methods
claim: A method is a sequence of stages: fit on prior data, iteratively sample and update, then output a valid estimate with confidence interval.
layout: 3 blocks left-to-right, central boxed loop with cyclic arrows and math inside
description: A horizontal flow diagram with three main parts. On the left, a rounded box labeled (a) 'Fit {u_i},{v_j} on historical data', captioned 'Historical Data'. A thick arrow labeled 'Initialize (û^(0), Σ̂^(0))' leads to a large rectangle captioned 'New Model', headed 'for t ∈ [1:n_b]:'. Inside it, three rounded boxes form a loop: (b) compute q_t(·) from the previous posterior, (c) sample question index I_t ~ q_t(·), and (d) observe label z_{I_t} and update (û^(t), Σ̂^(t)), with arrows cycling from b to c to d and back to b. A thick arrow on the right leads to a rounded box (e) with the formula θ̂ ± z_{1-α/2} σ̂/√n_b, captioned 'PAI Estimator + CI'. It is black and white, with math notation throughout. The eye goes first to the central loop.
caption: High-level overview of Factorized Active Querying (FAQ). (a) Using partially-observed historical outcomes H, we fit historical model and question factors (Eq. 6). For a new model, we initialize its latent factor from the historical fit. Then, at each sampling round t, we (b) compute the hybrid sampling policy qt(·) from the current factor posterior (Eq. 4), (c) sample a question It ∼qt(·), and (d) update the model factor using the observed outcome zIt (Eqs. 7-8). Finally, we (e) output the PAI estimate and confidence interval (Eqs. 2, 9).
abstract: Exhaustively evaluating many large language models (LLMs) on a large suite of benchmarks is expensive. We cast benchmarking as finite-population inference and, under a fixed query budget, seek tight confidence intervals (CIs) for model accuracy with asymptotic frequentist coverage. We propose Factorized Active Querying (FAQ), which (a) leverages historical information through a Bayesian factor model; (b) adaptively selects questions using a hybrid variance-reduction/active-learning sampling policy; and (c) maintains validity through Pro-Active Inference---a finite-population extension of active inference (Zrnic & CandÃ¨s, 2024) that enables direct question selection while preserving asymptotic frequentist coverage. In our experiments, FAQ delivers up to $5\times$ effective sample size gains over strong baselines on two benchmark suites, across varying historical-data missingness levels, with negligible computational overhead: this means that it matches the CI width of uniform sampling while using up to $5\times$ fewer queries. We release our source code and our curated datasets to support reproducibility and future research.
